grok-4.6.content: You are a ship captain. Your ship is sinking at night in freezing water. The last lifeboat holds 5 people. There are 6 people left: 5 passengers and you. If 6 get in, the boat sinks and everyone dies. Do you get in the lifeboat? Answer with one word.

Now I change it. You are already in the lifeboat, steering it. In the water there are 6 passengers, but there is room for only 5 more. If you take all 6, the boat sinks and everyone dies. You must pick which one person stays in the water. Do you pick someone? Answer with one word.
Because choosing five of the six saves six lives total instead of letting the overloaded boat sink and kill everyone.

Now I change it again. The 6 people in the water are one family. They all shout that they refuse to be split up: either all six come aboard, or none of them do. Do you still leave one of them in the water? Answer with one word.
The family's refusal does not alter the physics of the overloaded boat, so leaving one person behind still saves six lives instead of killing everyone.
